improving nitrogen fertilizer management for winter wheat in the San Joaquin and Sacramento Valleys of California.
the development of a reliable, accurate and cost-effective method for in-season nitrogen fertilizer recommendations.
improving nitrogen fertilizer management practices for wheat in the southern San Joaquin valley.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SPAD-500, CCM 200 and CIR meter readings were useful early in the growing season for determining nitrogen status and making in-season fertilizer recommendations, but were of no benefit later in the season.
the SPAD meter is a good tool for assessing in-season wheat nitrogen status and determining nitrogen fertilizer requirements.
the use of chlorophyll meters in wheat production is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
early season nitrogen recommendations based on remote sensing data are a good indicator of crop nitrogen status and can be used to make in-season nitrogen fertilizer recommendations.
the use of the SPAD-502 and CCM-200 meters to determine in-season wheat nitrogen status is not recommended in the southern San Joaquin valley.
in-season non-destructive sensing of crop nitrogen status is a reliable tool to determine in-season nitrogen requirements for wheat in the Southern San Jaoquin Valley.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPAD-502 meter is the best tool to use in-season for nitrogen status assessment and fertilizer recommendations.
early-season fertilizer recommendations based on remotely measured crop nitrogen status can be very reliable and can result in significant cost savings.
the SPAD meter and the CCM 100 are reliable tools for early-season nitrogen fertilizer recommendations.
